chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There was in the house of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) a fakhta (ring-dove). He heard it one day while it was shrieking, so he said to them: 'Do you know what this fakhta is saying?' They said, 'No.' He said: 'It is saying, I have lost you, I have lost you.' Then he said: 'We will lose it before it loses us.' Then he ordered for it to be slaughtered.

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَر: Abu Ja'far, referring to Imam Muhammad al-Baqir or Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the owner of the house.
key_terms.فَاخِتَة: A type of ring-dove, specifically mentioned in this hadith as a bird that was heard speaking or shrieking.
key_terms.لَنَفْقِدَنَّهَا: We will lose it, a prophetic statement by the Imam regarding the fate of the bird.

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the fakhta (ring-dove) in the house of Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Imam’s knowledge of the unseen (‘ilm al-ghayb) through the natural behavior of animals, a common theme in Shia hagiography. The linguistic play on the root 'f-q-d' (to lose) highlights the transient nature of worldly attachments, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on detachment from creation while maintaining stewardship. The narrative serves as a subtle reminder of divine providence and the temporary status of all creatures under human care.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, form Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There used to be in the house of Abu Ja’farasws, a Fakhta, so heasws heard it one days and it was shrieking. So heasws said to them: ‘Do you all know what it this Fakhta is saying?’ They said, ‘No’. Heasws said: ‘It is saying, ‘You are all lost, you are all lost!’ Then heasws said: ‘Weasws will lose it before it loses usasws’. Then heasws ordered for it to be slaughtered’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn af-Bakhtariy from a man who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

in the house of abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, there was al-Fakhtah and he one day heard it crying. He (the Imam) said, ‘Do you know what it (al-Fakhtah) says?’ They replied, ‘No, we do not know.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It says, ‘I have lost you, I have lost you.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘We will lose it before it will lose us.’ He (the Imam) commanded to slaughter it (for food).’”
